title: Wellington HE697 Memorial, Nederhorst den Berg
location_name: Nederhorst den Berg, North Holland, Netherlands
cause_of_loss: Shot down at 02:53 on 14 May 1943 by Oberleutnant Hans-Dieter Frank, 2. Staffel NJG 1. This was Frank's 31st aerial victory. Frank had claimed two further Wellington kills on the same night (kills 29 and 30), indicating an intensive operational period. Frank died on 28 September 1943, aged 24, after bailing out following a mid-air collision with another German nightfighter north-west of Celle.
memorial_details: A corten steel sculpture incorporating actual wreckage recovered from the crash site. The use of real aircraft material in the memorial structure is unusual among Commonwealth aircraft memorials in the Netherlands and indicates substantial wreckage recovery at the site. Unveiling date, sculptor, and exact location within the village have not been confirmed from accessible sources.
crew_summary: Wellington crew of six. No. 426 RCAF Squadron was based at RAF Dishforth in May 1943. Individual crew names, fates, and burial locations not yet confirmed.
narrative:
On the night of 13–14 May 1943, Wellington HE697 of No. 426 (Thunderbirds) Squadron RCAF was shot down at 02:53 approximately 10 kilometres north-west of Hilversum. The aircraft came down near Nederhorst den Berg, a village in the Vecht river area of North Holland.

The kill was claimed by Oberleutnant Hans-Dieter Frank of 2. Staffel, NJG 1. Wikipedia's account of Frank's kill record lists HE697 as his 31st aerial victory — the research brief stated 27th, but the Wikipedia source gives 31st; this discrepancy should be resolved against primary sources before this record is elevated to Comprehensive. Frank had also claimed two other Wellington kills earlier that same night (kills 29 and 30 on 13–14 May) and two more on 5 May 1943.

Frank was born on 8 July 1919 in Kiel and died on 28 September 1943, aged 24, after bailing out following a mid-air collision with another German nightfighter north-west of Celle. He was strangled by his radio cable.

The Nederhorst den Berg memorial incorporates actual wreckage from the crash site into a corten steel sculpture — a distinctive form of commemoration that speaks to the depth of local research and the physical evidence that survived at the site.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Hans-Dieter Frank (confirms HE697, 426 RCAF Sqn, kill date 14 May 1943 at 02:53, 10 km NW of Hilversum, kill number 31)
